lineage-proof-roadmap: This guide helps you: plan the chain of generations from you back to your patriot before you start filling in forms.
Start by: writing the chain first: every generation from you back to the patriot, names only.
Then: build an evidence grid for each generation in the Lineage Evidence Matrix.
substitute-evidence: This guide helps you: prove each generation without a birth certificate, using substitute records sorted by era.
Start by: dealing with any missing record in the three most recent generations, then the older links.
Then: enter each substitute in the Lineage Evidence Matrix and flag any record that disagrees.
read-pension-file: This guide helps you: find a pension file, decode its envelope and read its papers in the right order.
Start by: reading the selected records and any summary card or jacket first.
Then: test the file's marriage and service dates in the Widow Pension Law Checker.
records-by-state: This guide helps you: search for your ancestor's service records in the right repository.
Start by: identifying the type of service: Continental Army, state troops, militia, navy, or civil and patriotic service.
Then: record your patriot's service in the worksheet's patriot step.
bounty-land-warrants: This guide helps you: sort out what a bounty-land file shows about service and family, and where it misleads.
Start by: checking the proof-value table to see what the file can and cannot show.
Then: log any mismatch between the land and the family's home in the Lineage Evidence Matrix.
census-bridge: This guide helps you: work across the gap between a mid-1800s census and earlier censuses that name only the household head.
Start by: fixing the anchor: your ancestor's earliest census entry that lists every household member by name.
Then: record your estimates as indirect evidence in the Lineage Evidence Matrix.
patriotic-service: This guide helps you: prove service off the battlefield: committees, oaths, petitions, town office, supply taxes or furnished goods.
Start by: naming the service type and checking its window in the worksheet's patriot step.
Then: test your patriot's service dates in the worksheet's patriot step.
same-name: This guide helps you: prove that a service record with your ancestor's name is his, not another man's.
Start by: searching every spelling, then opening every same-name file for the state, not just the first.
Then: use the conflict flag in the Lineage Evidence Matrix for records that disagree.
patriot-or-loyalist: This guide helps you: test both sides of the record before you rely on a patriot claim.
Start by: building the patriot timeline: every dated act of service, with its source and place.
Then: enter each pro- and anti-independence record in the Lineage Evidence Matrix and flag conflicts.
application-problems: This guide helps you: find why a DAR or SAR application was questioned, and how to fix it.
Start by: assuming the problem is in the documentation, not the ancestor.
Then: run the Lineage Evidence Matrix report and clear every gap and conflict it lists.
